proof.text:
Write $\tau_t(h)=h(W,Z+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$ and $T=B[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$. Apply [lem-trf-formal-transverse-shift-calculus] with its parameter tuple $(W,Z)$, old transverse variables $V$, graph $\phi(W,Z)=Z$, no $T$ variables, and input $h(W,V)$ independent of the parameter copy of $Z$. The graph is in the parameter maximal ideal. Regrouping coefficient families identifies the output with $B[[Y]]$. The cited homomorphism and coefficient formula give $\tau_t$ as an $A$-algebra map and
$$[Y^\gamma]Y^\eta\tau_t(f_i)=\begin{cases}\partial_Z^{\gamma-\eta}f_i/(\gamma-\eta)!&\eta\le\gamma,\\0&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
All factorials are units in $L$. Only $Z$ is translated and differentiated.

proof.text: Let $M_t$ be the $B$-span of $\tau_t(h)$, $h\in J$. For each $j$, $Y_j\tau_t(h)=\tau_t(Z_jh)-Z_j\tau_t(h)$ lies in $M_t$, so it is a $T$-ideal. Each $\Delta_i$ is downward closed: $\eta\le\gamma\in\Delta_i$ and $\alpha_h\le\alpha_i+\eta$ with $h<i$ would imply $\alpha_h\le\alpha_i+\gamma$, a contradiction. For a supported expansion $h=\sum_iq_if_i$, the coefficient of $Y^\eta$ in $\tau_t(q_i)$ is $\sum_{\gamma\ge\eta}c_{i\gamma}(W)\binom\gamma\eta Z^{\gamma-\eta}$; it vanishes unless $\eta\in\Delta_i$. Each coefficient of $Z$ in this sum has one possible $\gamma$. Consequently $M_t$ is generated by the finite supported columns $Y^\eta\tau_t(f_i)$, $\eta\in\Delta_i$, $|\eta|\le t$. Conversely all these columns lie in $M_t$ by its $Y$-stability. The supported matrix $B'_t$ and the unrestricted $B_t^{\mathrm{rel}}$ therefore have the same image.

proof.text: Set $R_t=D\cap\{|\gamma|\le t\}$ and call supported columns with $|\eta|+d_i\le t$ good. The sets $\alpha_i+\Delta_i$ partition $D$ by assigning an exponent to its first dividing vertex, so there are exactly $r_t$ good columns. Reduce at $(W,Z)=0$. In homogeneous degree $k$, the initial forms $Y^\eta\operatorname{in}(\bar f_i)$, $|\eta|+d_i=k$, together with outside-$D$ monomials of degree $k$, are a basis by the full-prefix hypothesis. Ordered by degree, the truncated good columns and all outside-$D$ monomial columns form a square block triangular matrix with these invertible homogeneous diagonal blocks. It is invertible over $L$. Expanding along the outside monomial columns shows that the submatrix $C_t$ on good columns and rows $R_t$ has nonzero determinant at zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring](a), its determinant is a unit in $B=L[[W,Z]]$. The remaining supported columns vanish at zero, because $\bar f_i$ has order $d_i$. Thus both matrices have constant rank $r_t$.

source.place: Agent relative-coefficient proof; Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), determinant-expansion hint; source of the historical route is ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13. BM Theorem 7.14 archival PDF WANTED; no verbatim relative-coefficient theorem is claimed.

proof.text: Put $E=(\partial_Z^\nu f_i:|\nu|<d_i)$. A bad supported column has $|\eta|+d_i>t$; its nonzero entries in row $\gamma$ have derivative order $|\gamma-\eta|\le t-|\eta|<d_i$, so every entry belongs to $E$. Every selection of $r_t+1$ supported columns contains a bad one. Expand its determinant along that column using [lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula] with $s=1$: each summand has a factor in $E$. Hence all these minors are in $E$. Since the two matrices have equal column span, write $B_t^{\mathrm{rel}}=B'_tH$. For any selected square minor, [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] expresses it as a sum of products of minors of $B'_t$ with coefficients in $B$. The reverse inclusion of minor ideals follows because $B'_t$ is a submatrix. Therefore $I_t\subset E$ for every $t$, including oversized minors.

source.place: Agent relative-coefficient proof; Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), determinant-expansion hint; source of the historical route is ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13. BM Theorem 7.14 archival PDF WANTED; no verbatim relative-coefficient theorem is claimed.

proof.text:
For $t<d_i$ and $\gamma\notin D$, $|\gamma|\le t$, select the good columns and the extra column $(i,0)$, and the rows $R_t$ and the extra row $\gamma$. These are distinct, since $d_i>t$ and $\gamma\notin R_t$. The cofactor expansion in [lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula] has the term $\pm\det(C_t)\partial_Z^\gamma f_i/\gamma!$ at the extra row; every other term is a multiple of $\partial_Z^\alpha f_i/\alpha!$ for some $\alpha\in R_t$. Solving using the unit $\det C_t$ gives
$$\partial_Z^\gamma f_i\in I_t+(\partial_Z^\alpha f_i:\alpha\in D,\ |\alpha|\le t).$$
For $r_t=0$ the complementary determinant is $1$. Set $S_t=\sum_{u=0}^t I_u$, an increasing family; the same relation holds with $S_t$ in place of $I_t$.

proof.text: Let $k_1<\cdots<k_p$ be the distinct vertex degrees, $V_\ell=(Z_j:Z_j\in Z^\ell)$, and $V_0=0$. Induct on $\ell$, proving both $V_\ell\subset S_{k_\ell-1}$ and containment there of all lower transverse derivatives of generators in that prefix. Assume these for the previous block. If $d_i=k_\ell$ and $\alpha\in D$ with $|\alpha|<k_\ell$, a vertex dividing $\alpha$ has smaller degree, hence belongs to the previous prefix. Restrict $\alpha$ to $Z^{\ell-1}$, obtaining $\delta$ in that restricted prefix diagram; write $\alpha=\delta+\rho$, where $\rho$ uses only complementary variables. We have $|\delta|\le k_\ell-1\le Q$. The later-generator hypothesis gives $\partial^\delta f_i\in V_{\ell-1}$. Complementary derivatives preserve $V_{\ell-1}$ by the Leibniz rule, and partial derivatives commute by their coefficient formulas [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Therefore $\partial^\alpha f_i\in V_{\ell-1}\subset S_{k_\ell-1}$. For the first block there is no such $\alpha$.

proof.text:
For a current-block generator $f_i$ and any $|
u|<k_\ell$, step 6 handles $
u\in D$. For $
u
otin D$ apply step 5 with $t=k_\ell-1$; every supported derivative on its right is handled by step 6. Thus every lower derivative of the current block belongs to $S_{k_\ell-1}$; those from earlier blocks do by induction and monotonicity. In particular every chosen $g_j$ for this prefix is in $S_{k_\ell-1}$, since it is a derivative of order $d_{i(j)}-1$ of a generator already in the prefix. To recover $V_\ell$, use the graph-factorization clause of [lem-trf-formal-transverse-shift-calculus], with old transverse variables $Z^\ell$, complementary parameters $(W,Z\setminus Z^\ell)$, graph zero, and vector $(g_j)$. The assumptions $g_j\in V_\ell$ and invertible constant transverse Jacobian are exactly its hypotheses. It gives $(g_j)=V_\ell$, completing both induction claims. At the last block $E\subset S_{\max_i d_i-1}\subset S_Q$. Together with step 4, this proves the required equality.

proof.text: If there are no vertices, supported generation implies $J=0$; all columns and both ideals are zero. If there are no transverse variables, positive vertex degrees force this empty case. For nonempty vertices, each $k_\ell-1$ is nonnegative. Empty pivots were already handled by determinant $1$. No step used $\operatorname{ord}_{(W,Z)} f_i\ge d_i$: only the order of $\bar f_i$ was used, in step 3. Flatness is retained among the hypotheses; supported generation is assumed explicitly and suffices for this calculation.

proof.text: For any other finite generators $h_a$ of $J$, express each $h_a$ as a finite $B$-linear combination of the $f_i$ and conversely. Apply the ring homomorphism $\tau_t$ and expand its truncated coefficients in $Y$. The unrestricted monomial columns for the two families then span the same $M_t$. Cauchy--Binet [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] applied in both directions gives equality of their $(r_t+1)$-minor ideals, with the same fixed $r_t$. This establishes independence without any assumption that the replacement generators form a supported basis.

proof.text: Let $A\to A'$ be a continuous local coefficient homomorphism to a complete local coefficient ring, and extend it coefficientwise, fixing $Z,Y$. Coefficients of the Taylor matrix map to coefficients of the same Taylor matrix of the images: each is the integer-factor multiple of one derivative coefficient from step 1; continuity preserves the parameter-adic sums in those coefficients. Apply [lem-trf-row-minor-ideal-scalar-extension] to the row submodule generated by the transpose of $B_t^{\mathrm{rel}}$, with minor size $r_t+1$. It identifies the extended minor ideal with that generated by the mapped matrix. Equivalently each determinant is a finite integer polynomial in its entries. No flatness is needed for this compatibility. The index $r_t$ is held fixed; under a base change that alters a fibre diagram this is the base change of the original determinantal ideal, not a redefinition using a new rank.

proof.text: Work on an affine etale coordinate neighbourhood over a coefficient ring $R_0$, with coordinate algebra $R$, transverse coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_n$, and regular ideal generators $h_a$. Apply [lem-per-etale-relative-principal-parts-coordinates]. Under its isomorphism $P^t_{R/R_0}\simeq R[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$ the relation submodule generated by the ideal in the second factor has columns $Y^\eta T_t(h_a)$. Indeed $T_t$ is a ring map, so any expression $h=\sum a_ah_a$ translates to $T_t(h)=\sum T_t(a_a)T_t(h_a)$. These columns therefore present the quotient of the ambient principal-parts algebra by that relation submodule. The cited comparison sends them under a centered Taylor map to $Y^\eta f_a(W,Z+Y)$ with $f_a=\tau(h_a)$, fixing the coefficient variables. It also supplies this coordinate description after every coefficient base change, with no flatness hypothesis.

Take $(r_t+1)$-minors of the regular relation matrices of step 11, with the same prescribed index as their completed matrices. Equal generator spans give equal minor ideals by step 9's Cauchy--Binet argument. The coefficient map from the regular coordinate algebra to its centered Taylor algebra, or from $R_0$ to any $R'_0$, sends their row spans to the row spans of the compared matrices in step 11. The equality in [lem-trf-row-minor-ideal-scalar-extension] gives equality of the extended ideals and the compared minor ideals. Thus both centered Taylor expansion and arbitrary coefficient base change preserve these ideals. This concerns the image of the ideal in ambient principal parts; it does not assert that principal parts applied to the ideal injects into the ambient module.

title: Relative finite jet minors for a supported basis over complete coefficients
statement:
Let $L$ be a characteristic-zero field, $A=L[[W]]$, $B=A[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$, and $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subset B$ with $B/J$ flat over $A$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Fix a monotone transverse orthant diagram $D$ with ordered minimal vertices $\alpha_i$, $d_i=|\alpha_i|>0$, first-vertex quotient supports $\Delta_i$, and the accumulated essential variables $Z^\ell$ of each degree block [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Suppose $\bar f_i=f_i\bmod(W)$ has order $d_i$ and its initial forms have unique supported homogeneous division for every degree prefix. Suppose $J=\{\sum_iq_if_i:\operatorname{supp}_Zq_i\subseteq\Delta_i\}$. Choose $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$ in the first block containing $Z_j$. For every prefix, assume $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j}f_{i(j)}\in(Z^\ell)$ for $Z_j\in Z^\ell$, with invertible transverse Jacobian at $(W,Z)=0$. For later $i$ and every $\delta$ in the prefix diagram restricted to $Z^\ell$, $|\delta|\le Q$, assume $\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\delta}f_i\in(Z^\ell)$, where $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Form the relative finite Taylor matrix $B_t^{\mathrm{rel}}$ with columns $Y^\eta f_i(W,Z+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$, $|\eta|\le t$, in the monomial basis in $Y$, and put $r_t=\#\{\gamma\in D:|\gamma|\le t\}$. Let $I_t$ be its $(r_t+1)$-minor ideal [def-trf-minor-ideal]. Then
$$\sum_{t=0}^{Q} I_t=(\partial_Z^\nu f_i:|\nu|<d_i)\subset B.$$
The minor ideals are independent of the finite generators of $J$. They commute with continuous local changes of the complete coefficient ring fixing $Z$. In an etale smooth $N$-chart with section $Z=0$ and a coherent ideal, the same matrices are matrices of relative principal parts, formed from any regular generators; their minor ideals commute with centered Taylor expansion and arbitrary coefficient base change [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-coherent, def-trf-diagonal-jets]. Unlike the ordinary total-order version, no inequality $\operatorname{ord}_{(W,Z)}f_i\ge d_i$ is assumed.
